captures.description: THE CATALOGUE COUNTS EXACT, THE CONTROLS READ, IDENTITY LEFT UNASCERTAINED: asked for the arguments of The Ghost Catalogues (v0.5), grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1590 (chip: Goodreads ×1) through its two ghosts, 'one filing operation seen from its two sides': Thrasyllus's double titles (D.L. III.57–61) against the opening of Aristotle's catalogue (V.22), seventeen of twenty-six under the broad rule; the stricter controls, 9 of 26 (35%) against 6 of 118 (5%) and 9 of 214 (4%); the Divisions introduced 'διῄρει δέ, φησὶν Ἀριστοτέλης'; πειραστικός; the four-clause transform; the residue as 'the orthonym's footprint'; 'the immune response with a bibliography'; identity 'unascertainable in principle' without fragments, and the Rose and Ross test not run. It keeps the broad and strict counts apart and states what is not established.

atoms.evidence: Lee Sharks’s central argument in The Ghost Catalogues
The Ghost Catalogues: Aristotle's Lost Dialogues, Plato's Lost Divisions, and What a Two-Author Tradition Has to File as Missing (v0.5
Sharks makes the shape of the match the central datum and leaves the stronger identity claim unresolved.
Sharks begins with Diogenes Laertius III.57–61, which reports that Thrasyllus arranged Plato’s dialogues into tetralogies
In the introduction, Sharks calls the two ghosts “one filing operation seen from its two sides.”

The paper expressly declines to identify the hands responsible, establish dates, or choose conclusively between a single corpus, a school, a workshop, or another arrangement that could produce the observed pattern.
